data.description:
## Incident Overview

Subagents dispatched under the worktree-isolation protocol (see plugins/dso/skills/shared/prompts/worktree-dispatch.md) are observed writing to the session worktrees working directory instead of their own isolated sandbox worktree. This breaks the core isolation invariant the protocol is supposed to guarantee: each sub-agent should receive a sandboxed working directory independent of the orchestrators directory, and the orchestrator is solely responsible for merging back via single-agent-integrate.md / harvest-worktree.sh.

When the invariant fails, sub-agent edits land directly on the session branch without going through:
- the per-worktree review / commit gate
- the test gate
- the merge-back harvest
- the WORKTREE_TRACKING:complete ledger

This can corrupt the session branch, bypass review, and leave orphaned in-flight changes from concurrent sub-agents racing on the same files.

## Observed scope

User reports observing the violation across multiple sessions and across multiple skills (fix-bug single-agent dispatch, sprint multi-agent dispatch, debug-everything). No single deterministic reproduction is in hand; the symptom appears intermittently.

## Expected behavior

Per worktree-dispatch.md Step 2: every Agent/Task dispatch passes isolation: "worktree" and the sub-agents Git Root Verification check (SUB_AGENT_ROOT vs ORCHESTRATOR_ROOT) HARD-FAILS (exit 1) if they match. The invariant should be: it is impossible for a sub-agent to write to the orchestrators worktree because (a) the Agent tool gives it a distinct cwd, and (b) the sub-agent itself verifies and exits 1 on mismatch.

## Actual behavior

Sub-agent edits are landing in the session worktree path. Possible mechanisms (to be confirmed by investigation):
1. Dispatch sites that omit isolation: "worktree" from the Agent tool parameters
2. Dispatch sites that omit ORCHESTRATOR_ROOT injection in the prompt, allowing the sub-agents own guard to short-circuit
3. Sub-agents that do not run the Git Root Verification snippet as their first action
4. A Claude Code Agent tool behavior where isolation: "worktree" silently degrades to shared cwd
5. Sub-agents using absolute paths back into the orchestrator root (path injection escape)

## Reproduction

To be determined by investigation. User has no concrete log/commit evidence; investigation should start by auditing all Agent/Task dispatch sites in the dso plugin against the worktree-dispatch.md contract, then construct a probe that detects whether isolation is actually in effect at runtime.

## Severity rationale

High: this is a load-bearing safety invariant. When it fails, the session branch can receive un-reviewed, un-tested writes; review-gate hashes can be invalidated mid-batch; concurrent sub-agents can race on the same files in the session worktree.
data.title: [worktree-dispatch protocol]: subagents using worktree isolation -> writes land in session worktree instead of isolated sandbox
